title: MMACHC burden variants are associated with higher circulating vitamin B12 in the All of Us cohort.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC record (PMID 42822437; AJHG vol. 113 issue 10; authors Cai L, DeBerardinis RJ): not open access, no PMCID, no abstract, no supplement, no text-mined accessions, no NCBI (National Center for Biotechnology Information) links, no Zenodo/Dryad deposit. The All of Us data-access page states that individual-level data are available only to registered researchers on the Researcher Workbench.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Nothing beyond the title: no abstract or full text was retrievable. The claim that the analysis uses All of Us whole genomes linked to serum vitamin B12 lab values is inferred from the title.

a1_downloadable.note: All of Us individual-level genomes and lab values need Researcher Workbench registration, and genomic data sit in the Controlled Tier; this is an access application, so it fails. Checked on the All of Us data-access page.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked: no files are accessible. The label would be B12 values pulled from health-record lab tables, which would have to be constructed (unit harmonisation, picking one measurement per person, excluding supplement users).

a3_inputs_present.note: Not checked; inputs would be per-person variant calls inside the Workbench, which can't be exported.

a5_enough_rows.note: Row count unknown; the paper text was not retrievable.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Analysis must run in the cloud Workbench; it can't be done on the laptop.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Can't compare: no paper text and no files.

a8_label_provenance.note: Per the title, the label would be a clinically measured serum vitamin B12 level, not a model output. Not verified.

honest_claim_h3: None possible: the data are behind All of Us controlled access and the paper is not open access.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a person's rare damaging variants in the MMACHC gene to predict their blood vitamin B12 level.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-person genetic variants plus demographics for All of Us participants who have a B12 lab test; the number of people is unknown.
plain_idea.predict: Circulating vitamin B12 concentration, taken from clinical lab results in electronic health records.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It could flag carriers whose B12 readings are misleading. The paper itself is a gene-level association study, not an ML dataset.

label_elsewhere.sources: UK Biobank has no routine B12 measurement; published B12 GWAS (genome-wide association study) summary statistics exist (known resource, not searched here).
label_elsewhere.why: Not filled in detail because the verdict is reject.

ml_idea: Gene-burden association analysis on controlled-access biobank data; no openly downloadable table, so it is not a laptop ML project.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: the data can't leave the All of Us cloud Workbench.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Is there any open supplement with per-variant B12 effect sizes? None was found in Europe PMC (no PMCID, no supplement).

verdict_reason: A1 fails: All of Us individual-level genomes and lab values need Researcher Workbench registration (genomes are Controlled Tier). The paper is paywalled with no PMCID, abstract, supplement or deposited data.
